1.title: Services and Pod Connectivity
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Services and Pod Connectivity. It covers the exam area Services and Networking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Understand connectivity between Pods. Use Cluster I P, Node Port, Load Balancer service types and endpoints. Practice with eight hands-on labs worth forty points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Services and Networking (twenty percent). Practice in this module: eight labs, forty points, about forty minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero (kind net C N I (Container Network Interface).

1.title: The networking rules of Kubernetes
1.text: The networking rules of Kubernetes. Every Pod gets its own I P address. Pods can reach every other Pod by I P, on any node, without nat (unless a Network Policy blocks it). Nodes can reach all Pods and Pods can reach all nodes. Pod I P s are not stable: a replaced Pod gets a new I P. A Service gives a stable virtual I P and name in front of a changing set of Pods. The C N I plugin (Module one) builds the Pod network; kube proxy on each node turns Service I P s into Pod I P s. Find I P s and nodes: kube control get pods dash o wide. One Pod's I P: kube control get pod p dash o json path dot status dot pod I P.

1.title: Service types
1.text: Service types. Cluster I P (default). Reachable from: inside the cluster. How: virtual I P plus D N S name. Use: internal services. Node Port. Reachable from: outside via any node I P node Port. How: opens the same port (thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven by default) on every node, on top of a Cluster I P. Use: simple external access, tests. Load Balancer. Reachable from: outside via a cloud address. How: asks the cloud for a load balancer; builds on Node Port. Use: production on a cloud. External Name. Reachable from: inside. How: D N S alias (C N A M E) to an outside host; no proxy, no selector. Use: pointing at an external database. Headless ( cluster I P None ). Reachable from: inside. How: D N S returns Pod I P s directly. Use: Stateful Sets. Exam tip: Node Port uses the range thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven.

1.title: Service types, continued
1.text: Service types. A Service has a selector (which Pods) and ports. port. the port clients use on the Service. target Port. the port on the Pod's container (defaults to port ). node Port. the port opened on every node (Node Port and Load Balancer only).

1.title: Service types, continued
1.text: Service types. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Service types, continued
1.text: Service types. kube control expose copies the selector from the object it exposes and names the Service after it unless the name flag is given. To choose a node port, generate yamel with the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, add node Port thirty thousand eighty under the port, and apply (Lab seven point two). In the lab cluster, a Load Balancer Service never gets an external address ( pending ) because there is no cloud. On the exam, cloud behavior depends on the environment; the Service definition is what you create.

1.title: Endpoints: what a Service actually points at
1.text: Endpoints: what a Service actually points at. A Service sends traffic only to Ready Pods that match its selector. The list of those Pod I P s is held in Endpoint Slice objects (the older Endpoints object still exists but is deprecated). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A Service with no endpoints points to a selector, readiness or port problem: check those three.

1.title: Endpoints: what a Service actually points at, continued
1.text: Endpoints: what a Service actually points at. No endpoints equals the Service cannot work. The three causes, in order of frequency. The Service selector does not match the Pod labels (a typo; Lab seven point three). The Pods are not Ready (failing readiness probe, crash loop). target Port is wrong: endpoints exist but connections are refused. Debug in this order: kube control get svc,endpointslices, kube control get pods the show labels flag, kube control describe svc, then kube control exec into a client Pod and W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash svc.

1.title: Service DNS names
1.text: Service D N S names. Core D N S gives every Service a name: service. namespace dot svc dot cluster dot local. same namespace. shop. other namespace. shop dot svc one or the full name. Exam tip: From another namespace, reach a Service as service. namespace.

1.title: Service DNS names, continued
1.text: Service D N S names. A Pod's slash E T C slash resolv dot conf has a search path ( ns dot svc dot cluster dot local svc dot cluster dot local cluster dot local ) and nameserver set to the D N S Service I P. Services get the A record; headless Services return every Pod I P; Stateful Set Pods get pod-zero dot service dot ns dot svc dot cluster dot local. Cross-namespace access needs only the right name (Lab seven point seven). More on D N S in Module eight.

1.title: How Services work on the node (short)
1.text: How Services work on the node (short). kube proxy watches Services and Endpoint Slices and writes rules (I P tables, I P V S or nftables mode) so that traffic to the Cluster I P is randomly forwarded to one ready Pod I P. The Cluster I P is virtual: it is not on any interface, so you cannot ping it; test with the Service port using W get or curl. If Service traffic fails on one node only, check that node's kube proxy Pod (Module thirteen).

1.title: A fast way to test connectivity
1.text: A fast way to test connectivity. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Test from inside the cluster with a busy box Pod and W get -q O- -T three.

1.title: A fast way to test connectivity, continued
1.text: A fast way to test connectivity. the rm flag dash i the restart flag set to Never runs a throw-away Pod and removes it. -T three makes W get give up after three seconds so a blocked path fails quickly.

1.title: Lab 7.1: clusterip service
1.text: Lab seven point one: clusterip service. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc one, the Deployment shop (two replicas, engine X alpine, listening on port eighty) exists. Create a Service named shop of type Cluster I P that is reachable inside the cluster on port eighty eighty and forwards to the containers' port eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 7.1: clusterip service, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc one expose deployment shop the port flag set to eighty eighty the target port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n svc one get svc shop. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 7.2: nodeport service
1.text: Lab seven point two: nodeport service. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc two, expose the Deployment web (engine X on port eighty) with a Service named web np of type Node Port, service port eighty, using the fixed node port thirty thousand eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 7.2: nodeport service, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc two expose deployment web the name flag set to web np the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Node Port the dry run flag set, and so on. Then sed dash i s or - port eighty or - port eighty newline node Port thirty thousand eighty or slash tmp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two apply dash f slash tmp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two get svc web np. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 7.3: fix service selector
1.text: Lab seven point three: fix service selector. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc three, the Service api does not work: requests to H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three hang. The Deployment api (two replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.3: fix service selector, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc three get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name api. Then kube control dash n svc three get svc api dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n svc three get pods the show labels flag. Then kube control dash n svc three patch svc api dash p spec selector app api. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.4: endpoint ips
2.text: Lab seven point four: endpoint ips. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc four, the Service db is backed by several Pods. Write the I P addresses of all Pods that currently serve the Service (one I P per line, sorted) to about slash answers slash endpoints dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.4: endpoint ips, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name db. Then kube control dash n svc four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name db dash o json path range dot items dot endpoints dot addresses zero newline end sort about slash, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.5: loadbalancer service
2.text: Lab seven point five: loadbalancer service. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc five, expose the Deployment front (engine X, port eighty) with a Service named front lb of type Load Balancer on port eighty. In this test cluster there is no cloud load balancer, so the external address stays pending; only the Service definition is checked. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.5: loadbalancer service, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc five expose deployment front the name flag set to front lb the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Load Balancer. Then kube control dash n svc five get svc front lb. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.6: externalname
2.text: Lab seven point six: externalname. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc six, create a Service named legacy db that makes the name legacy db dot svc six dot svc dot cluster dot local resolve (as a D N S alias) to the external host db dot example dot com. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.6: externalname, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc six create service externalname legacy db the external name flag set to db dot example dot com. Then kube control dash n svc six get svc legacy db. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.7: cross namespace dns
2.text: Lab seven point seven: cross namespace dns. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The Pod server (engine X) runs in the namespace back and the Pod client (busy box) runs in the namespace front. Make the client able to fetch the engine X page from the server by the name H T T P colon slash slash server dot back (do not touch the Pods). Then write the full D N S name of the Service (including dot svc dot cluster dot local ) to about slash answers slash fqdn dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.7: cross namespace dns, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n back expose pod server the port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n front exec client -- W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash server dot back then pipe to head -three. Then echo server dot back dot svc dot cluster dot local about slash answers slash fqdn dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 7.8: multiport service
2.text: Lab seven point eight: multiport service. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc eight, the Deployment app (two replicas) has Pods that listen on port eighty (web) and eighty eighty (metrics; the image is engine X so only eighty answers, the definition is what counts). Create a Service named app that exposes two named ports: http on port eighty targeting container port eighty, and metrics on port nine thousand ninety targeting container port eighty eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 7.8: multiport service, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n svc eight apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n svc eight get svc app. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which two properties of Pod I P s make a Service necessary? Answer: Pod I P s change when Pods are replaced, and a workload has many Pods; a Service gives one stable name and I P. Question two. What is the difference between port and target Port? Answer: port is what clients use on the Service; target Port is the container port traffic is sent to. Question three. Which node port range is the default for Node Port Services? Answer: thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. A Service has no endpoints. What do you check first? Answer: That the Service selector matches the Pod labels ( kube control get pods the show labels flag ), then that the Pods are Ready. Question five. Which Service type creates a D N S alias to an outside host? Answer: External Name. Question six. What is the full D N S name of Service api in namespace prod? Answer: api dot prod dot svc dot cluster dot local.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Why does ping Cluster I P fail even when the Service works? Answer: The Cluster I P is virtual (kube proxy rules); only the Service ports answer. Question eight. Which object holds the Pod I P s behind a Service? Answer: Endpoint Slices (older Endpoints is deprecated).

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Types: Cluster I P, Node Port (thirty thousand to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-seven), Load Balancer, External Name, headless. Expose: kube control expose... the port flag the target port flag the type flag the name flag. Endpoints: kube control get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name svc; empty equals selector, readiness or port problem. D N S: svc. ns dot svc dot cluster dot local; svc. ns from another namespace. Test: busy box W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash svc from a Pod. Pod network: every Pod has an I P; Pods reach Pods without nat. In the next module, we continue the course.
